A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ORC-MANL research. Their main texts and appendices contain readable equations, proofs, tables, and figures sufficient for reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic pruning experiments, downstream geometric analyses, scRNAseq experiments, and empirical convergence results.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds MNIST/KMNIST results, runtime measurements, and parameter ablations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same curvature screening and graph-distance validation steps and thresholds. Replacing uniform edge weights of epsilon with 1 for ORC computation is mathematically equivalent: the common scaling cancels in the Wasserstein-to-distance ratio. Explicit Euclidean weighting elsewhere clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Section 4.2.2 adds actual evaluation on MNIST and KMNIST, extending coverage from synthetic manifolds and scRNAseq to image data. Existing datasets remain; synthetic spectral clustering moves from v1 Appendix A.4.2 to v2 Section 4.1.5.

E2.justification: The pruning comparisons retain ORC ONLY, BISECTION, MST, DENSITY, and DISTANCE. V2 Appendix A.2 newly evaluates UMAP as a runtime comparator against ORC-MANL; its earlier participation was in downstream embedding experiments.

E3.justification: V2 introduces controlled parameter sweeps on 4,000-point samples, runtime evaluation across sample sizes, and inter-/intra-class edge-removal measurements on 10,000-image datasets. Appendix A.3.3 also revises the displayed intrinsic-dimension estimator by adding a reciprocal; this documents a correction without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.5.1 systematically tests sensitivity to k, delta, and lambda on four synthetic manifolds, exposing parameter-dependent shortcut retention and removal of good edges. Appendix A.2 adds empirical runtime scaling. Earlier convergence, curvature, and repeated t-SNE analyses remain.

E5.justification: V1 Section 4.1.1 explicitly identifies ten trials and mean/standard-deviation reporting for the pruning table; v2 omits that explanation while retaining the numerical uncertainties. New Table 5 explicitly uses ten seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting, continuing the earlier practice rather than demonstrating increased replication.

E6.justification: V2 adds image-data, runtime, and ablation results. MNIST inter-/intra-class removal is 14.92%/7.90%, and KMNIST is 14.70%/5.39%. Intrinsic-dimension MSEs change between v1 Figure 6 and v2 Figure 8: pruned/unpruned Swiss-roll values change from 0.026/0.053 to 0.031/0.069, and sphere values from 0.004/0.006 to 0.0026/0.0044. Original pruning-table scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds a runtime-complexity derivation in Appendix A.2 and corrects the intrinsic-dimension estimator's missing reciprocal. Theorem 3.2's proof sketch replaces almost-sure convergence language with high-probability statements. The principal theorem statements and substantive proof development remain intact.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same claims: theoretically justified shortcut pruning using ORC and graph distances, superiority to pruning baselines, and benefits for downstream geometric analysis. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 cautions that class-crossing edges are not necessarily geometric shortcuts, interprets the new runtime results as supporting practicality, and adds a pointwise-versus-global estimator bias argument. It removes v1's clustering caveat about disconnected graphs producing infinite pairwise distances for UMAP/t-SNE inputs.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the timing machine's 16 cores and 187 GB RAM, implementation sources, multiprocessing, and ablation controls. It clarifies graph weighting and corrects BISECTION's documented midpoint from (x-y)/2 to (x+y)/2, without establishing a changed implementation. The GitHub code link already appears in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for MNIST, KMNIST, and the UMAP software implementation. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to graph pruning and curvature-based methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 expands explanations of distances, weighting, and thresholds, moves clustering into the main text, and subdivides the real-data section. It also updates affiliations, publication headers, and terminology. Most existing prose and the overall theoretical narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats the displays: the original pruning table and pruning visualization are each split, many figures are enlarged or reframed, and mathematical statements receive shaded boxes. It adds the manifold-parameter schematic, image-data and runtime figures, and ablation table, while relocating the existing clustering figure.

improvement.justification: The new sensitivity and runtime analyses address practical questions absent from v1, while image-data experiments broaden validation with an appropriate limitation on class-based interpretation. Formula corrections and clearer figures also help. These gains are tempered by weaker documentation of the original pruning table's uncertainty and an apparent erroneous 100.0 ± 100.0 percentage entry in Table 5. Overall, v2 provides a useful but qualified improvement.
